notes.1: ...c6 prepares ...d5 and keeps the c8 bishop's diagonal open.
notes.5: The point of the Caro-Kann: the bishop gets out before ...e6 locks it in.
notes.7: Now ...e6 is fine. The light-squared bishop is already outside the pawn chain.
notes.9: ...c5 hits the base of White's d4–e5 chain.

notes.5: Take back with the c-pawn. The structure is symmetrical, but you get the half-open c-file.
notes.7: Develop and add pressure on d4.
notes.9: Nf6 controls e4 and gets the king ready to castle.
notes.11: Get the bishop out actively before ...e6 locks it in. Watch out: with it gone from c8, b7 is loose and Qb3 hits it.

notes.5: Give up the center for now in exchange for fast, easy development.
notes.7: Develop the bishop with tempo on the e4 knight.
notes.9: Keep the bishop on the diagonal. It retreats but doesn't go passive.
notes.11: ...h6 makes room so the bishop can go to h7 when h5 comes.
notes.13: Nd7 stops White's Ne5 from hitting g6.
notes.15: The bishop is safe on h7 and still aims at White's queenside.
